evidence.claim: The official bio states that Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo has been President of the Republic since 24 January 2019 and was elected on 30 December 2018.
evidence.title: Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo - Présidence RDC
evidence.excerpt: The official bio states that Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo has been President of the Republic since 24 January 2019 and was elected on 30 December 2018.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential biography; direct office-identification source.
evidence.period_fit: Direct office confirmation for the 2022 ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Official self-description of the office holder; useful for identity and tenure only.
contrary_evidence: Self-published and favorable; not independent verification of performance.

evidence.claim: Vidiye Tshimanga, described as one of Tshisekedi's closest advisers, was recorded offering mining licenses and protection from bribe-seeking officials in exchange for a stake, and he described hiding the share through proxies and offshore trusts.
evidence.title: I Will Take My Percentage: Congolese Presidential Adviser Caught on Tape Negotiating Corrupt Mineral Deal
evidence.excerpt: Vidiye Tshimanga, described as one of Tshisekedi's closest advisers, was recorded offering mining licenses and protection from bribe-seeking officials in exchange for a stake, and he described hiding the share through proxies and offshore trusts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Investigative reporting with named reporters, direct recording excerpts, and follow-up confirmation from the subject, though the tape-makers were unidentified.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and centered on a senior member of Tshisekedi's governing circle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the conduct is by a presidential adviser who repeatedly invoked his proximity to Tshisekedi; this is not proof Tshisekedi personally took money.
contrary_evidence: Tshimanga denied wrongdoing and said he was being set up; OCCRP could not identify who made the recordings.

evidence.claim: Le Temps reported that Tshimanga resigned after the investigation and said the later audio excerpts he supplied did not invalidate his earlier statements about offshore structures or acting on the president's behalf.
evidence.title: Un haut responsable congolais demissionne a la suite des revelations du Temps
evidence.excerpt: Le Temps reported that Tshimanga resigned after the investigation and said the later audio excerpts he supplied did not invalidate his earlier statements about offshore structures or acting on the president's behalf.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Swiss investigative reporting on the same video evidence, with a clear note that later excerpts did not erase the earlier admissions.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly about the same resignation and taped meetings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect through a cabinet-level aide who referenced the presidency and the president's campaign.
contrary_evidence: Tshimanga said the material was a trap and that his remarks were taken out of context.

evidence.claim: The presidency said Tshisekedi's state-of-the-nation speech reviewed efforts on anti-corruption, universal health coverage, education, youth entrepreneurship, public revenue mobilization, elections, and public administration modernization.
evidence.title: Discours du President de la Republique Felix Tshisekedi sur l'etat de la nation
evidence.excerpt: The presidency said Tshisekedi's state-of-the-nation speech reviewed efforts on anti-corruption, universal health coverage, education, youth entrepreneurship, public revenue mobilization, elections, and public administration modernization.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official speech text is reliable for what was said, but it is self-report rather than independent proof of implementation or honesty.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct self-presentation by Tshisekedi, but it is not independent verification.
contrary_evidence: It is a promotional summary, not an external finding that the claims were true or fully implemented.

evidence.claim: The IMF report said the DRC program was based on Tshisekedi's vision and recommended stronger governance and transparency measures, including beneficial-ownership disclosure in procurement, an asset-declaration regime for politically exposed persons and close associates, and independent anti-corruption institutions.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo Staff Report for the 2022 Article IV Consultation, Second Review under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement
evidence.excerpt: The IMF report said the DRC program was based on Tshisekedi's vision and recommended stronger governance and transparency measures, including beneficial-ownership disclosure in procurement, an asset-declaration regime for politically exposed persons and close associates, and independent anti-corruption institutions.
evidence.source_locator: Appendix I, Letter of Intent para. 1; governance recommendations table on business environment, governance and corruption
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent IMF country report with explicit governance recommendations and a direct statement of the authorities' program frame.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly about the Tshisekedi government’s program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: this is the external reform agenda for the Tshisekedi administration, not proof of Tshisekedi's personal honesty.
contrary_evidence: Recommendations imply gaps in current practice; they do not prove clean personal conduct.

evidence.claim: The 2022-2026 Country Partnership Framework supports the DRC government’s strategic priorities, emphasizes human development and stronger basic services, and targets poor, vulnerable, and conflict-affected people through a countrywide social safety net.
evidence.title: World Bank Deepens Commitment to Building Human Capital and Inclusive Development in the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: The 2022-2026 Country Partnership Framework supports the DRC government’s strategic priorities, emphasizes human development and stronger basic services, and targets poor, vulnerable, and conflict-affected people through a countrywide social safety net.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank press release with dated, explicit program language and financing details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: the document reflects government strategic priorities under Tshisekedi, but implementation is jointly shaped by World Bank financing and technical design.
contrary_evidence: The same release says poverty is rising and governance is weak, so this is an agenda and financing framework rather than proof of delivery.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi chaired an evaluation meeting on the 145-territories development program; officials said the identified projects were ready and the plan would build hospitals, administrative buildings, and other infrastructure across the country.
evidence.title: Réunion d'évaluation du programme de développement à la base des 145 territoires présidée ce jour par le chef de l'état.
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi chaired an evaluation meeting on the 145-territories development program; officials said the identified projects were ready and the plan would build hospitals, administrative buildings, and other infrastructure across the country.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential page with a dated meeting summary and concrete project description.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the source attributes the meeting to Tshisekedi and reports his oversight of the program, though completion is not shown.
contrary_evidence: The page says projects were ready and the launch was imminent, which shows preparation more than completed delivery.

evidence.claim: ANSER launched 11 tenders for the PDL-145 rural electrification component, including three hydroelectric plants and eight solar photovoltaic plants in specific territories.
evidence.title: ANSER lance un nouveau lot d’avis d’appels d’offres relatifs au volet électrification du PDL-145 au profit du Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Nord-Ubangi et l’espace Grand Kasaï
evidence.excerpt: ANSER launched 11 tenders for the PDL-145 rural electrification component, including three hydroelectric plants and eight solar photovoltaic plants in specific territories.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local reporting with a specific procurement announcement and concrete project list.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct but partial: the article ties the tenders to the president’s development vision, but execution still depends on procurement and implementation follow-through.
contrary_evidence: Tenders are not completed projects; the article shows procurement initiation rather than finished electrification.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi praised the creation of a National Solidarity and Humanitarian Catastrophe Management Fund, ordered the government to equip it with adequate resources, and pushed a formal monitoring mechanism for the prevention-resilience strategy.
evidence.title: Compte rendu de la soixante-seizième réunion du Conseil des Ministres
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi praised the creation of a National Solidarity and Humanitarian Catastrophe Management Fund, ordered the government to equip it with adequate resources, and pushed a formal monitoring mechanism for the prevention-resilience strategy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential council minutes with explicit instructions and institutional follow-up steps.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the source records Tshisekedi’s own instructions to the government, though it still shows setup and coordination more than delivered outcomes.
contrary_evidence: The source is mainly about creating mechanisms and ordering reports; it does not prove the fund had materially improved outcomes by year-end.

evidence.claim: After the swearing-in of 73 magistrates, Tshisekedi stressed serving the nation rather than themselves, reaffirmed judicial independence, and ordered public-finance governance and payroll reforms.
evidence.title: Compte rendu de la soixante-septième réunion du Conseil des Ministres
evidence.excerpt: After the swearing-in of 73 magistrates, Tshisekedi stressed serving the nation rather than themselves, reaffirmed judicial independence, and ordered public-finance governance and payroll reforms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential communication with a dated, specific institutional directive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the source quotes Tshisekedi’s instructions and reform emphasis, though downstream implementation is not independently demonstrated here.
contrary_evidence: This shows directive-setting, not completed implementation or measurable results.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $300 million project to support women entrepreneurs and MSMEs, create up to 2,500 formal firms, improve access for up to 25,000 women entrepreneurs, and contribute to a projected 28,000 jobs.
evidence.title: Empowering Women Entrepreneurs to Boost Economic Transformation in the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a $300 million project to support women entrepreneurs and MSMEs, create up to 2,500 formal firms, improve access for up to 25,000 women entrepreneurs, and contribute to a projected 28,000 jobs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official development-bank release with quantified outputs and ministry supervision details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: the project is aligned to the DRC government’s economic transformation agenda, but the direct implementer and financing are heavily external and the jobs are projected, not yet realized.
contrary_evidence: The claimed jobs and firm creation are projections over five years, so the article shows planned capacity rather than completed 2022 outcomes.

evidence.claim: Despite robust growth, poverty reduction remained elusive and growth benefits were not widely shared, while the DRC faced a stark digital divide and major geographic and socio-economic disparities in access.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Economic Update: Harnessing Growth Through Digital Connectivity to Create Jobs and Reduce Poverty
evidence.excerpt: Despite robust growth, poverty reduction remained elusive and growth benefits were not widely shared, while the DRC faced a stark digital divide and major geographic and socio-economic disparities in access.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank update summarizing observed 2022 conditions with specific country findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: these are national outcomes during Tshisekedi’s tenure, but the article itself emphasizes inherited constraints, external shocks, and structural issues.
contrary_evidence: Robust growth and resilience to shocks complicate any simple claim of overall failure.

evidence.claim: The government liberalized the telecommunications sector through a new Telecommunications Law with a modern regulatory environment and a universal access goal, but the report said secondary legislation was still needed to operationalize it.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Economic Update: Harnessing Growth Through Digital Connectivity to Create Jobs and Reduce Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The government liberalized the telecommunications sector through a new Telecommunications Law with a modern regulatory environment and a universal access goal, but the report said secondary legislation was still needed to operationalize it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank update with a concrete policy description and explicit implementation gap.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct but partial: the reform is credited to the government, yet the report explicitly says execution still required enabling legislation and follow-through.
contrary_evidence: The need for secondary legislation means the reform was incomplete in 2022.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the authorities adopted prudent macroeconomic policies, most visibly by halting central bank financing to the government, and that scaling up structural reforms remained critical for inclusive growth and the business climate.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Staff Report for the 2022 Article IV Consultation, Second Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement, Request for Modifications of Performance Criteria, and Financing Assurances Review
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the authorities adopted prudent macroeconomic policies, most visibly by halting central bank financing to the government, and that scaling up structural reforms remained critical for inclusive growth and the business climate.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF country report with explicit macro-policy assessment and reform agenda.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: the macro-policy change is attributable to the Tshisekedi government, but the report also stresses structural constraints and the continuing need for reform.
contrary_evidence: The same report says additional reforms were still needed, so the improvement was real but incomplete.

evidence.claim: Kinshasa launched an accelerated COVID-19 vaccination campaign targeting at least 11 million people between April and June 2022, but official data still showed only 890,363 first-dose vaccinations as of 7 April 2022, and the rollout relied on mobile and fixed vaccination sites.
evidence.title: Vaccinodromes, équipes mobiles : la RDC accélère sa campagne de vaccination contre la COVID-19 ciblant 11 millions de personnes entre avril et juin 2022
evidence.excerpt: Kinshasa launched an accelerated COVID-19 vaccination campaign targeting at least 11 million people between April and June 2022, but official data still showed only 890,363 first-dose vaccinations as of 7 April 2022, and the rollout relied on mobile and fixed vaccination sites.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official WHO regional note with explicit baseline, target, and operational design details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: the campaign is government-led but partner-supported, and the low starting coverage shows the scale of the challenge rather than completed success.
contrary_evidence: The target was ambitious and the baseline was very low, so the source shows an effort to catch up rather than achieved vaccination coverage.

evidence.claim: A new $250 million grant was set to improve access to community infrastructure and reintegration programs for 3.3 million people in eastern provinces, with provincial-level implementation and substantial funding for capacity-building, income generation, and psychosocial and mental health services.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of Congo: World Bank Approves $250 Million to Improve Stability and Resilience in Conflict-Affected Eastern Provinces
evidence.excerpt: A new $250 million grant was set to improve access to community infrastructure and reintegration programs for 3.3 million people in eastern provinces, with provincial-level implementation and substantial funding for capacity-building, income generation, and psychosocial and mental health services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank press release with precise beneficiary counts, funding, and implementation design.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: the project is aligned with the government’s renewed commitment to stabilization, but actual results depend on provincial implementation and donor execution.
contrary_evidence: This is a newly approved grant, so it indicates mobilization and design rather than realized stabilization by year-end.

evidence.claim: The DRC increased its 2023 budget to $16 billion, up from a proposed $14.6 billion in September, with the final increase attributed to revenue mobilization and higher mining prices.
evidence.title: Congo increases budget 46% for 2023, boosted by taxes
evidence.excerpt: The DRC increased its 2023 budget to $16 billion, up from a proposed $14.6 billion in September, with the final increase attributed to revenue mobilization and higher mining prices.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting syndicated through MarketScreener with explicit budget numbers and attribution, though not a primary government text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: revenue mobilization by government services is cited, but commodity prices also helped drive the increase.
contrary_evidence: Part of the increase came from mining price improvement, so the budget gain is not purely evidence of ruler skill.

unresolved_gaps: No direct evidence of nuclear command-and-control, custody, accident-prevention, or safety-safeguard performance under Tshisekedi.
Independent compliance evidence for the Nairobi and Luanda processes remains thin.
Direct command-responsibility evidence and remedy follow-up for police and military abuses are still weak.
Direct evidence on institutional strengthening, political equality, and election-body independence is thin.
Independent 2022 implementation and household-level outcome evidence is still thin.
Direct ruler-attributable outcome data on health, education, nutrition, and protection remains sparse.
Direct evidence of Tshisekedi's own assets, family/business interests, campaign finance, and false statements is missing.
Completed outputs and adaptation under failure are not well documented for the major 2022 programs.
